summary: Unexpected forfeiture of retained credits after account consolidation
description: Issue summary: After a customer-initiated org consolidation on 2026-03-09 (merging two sub-orgs into a single paid org), Brightline Freight reports that a block of retained hourly reserve credits (~48h worth) that previously appeared on the source subaccount vanished from the consolidated invoice and account balance. Impact: customer is short ~$4.2k of usable credits which they relied on for a scheduled batch embedding job. They requested urgent review before finance closes the billing cycle. Environment: production, us-east region, dedicated reserved capacity. Observed behavior: credits were visible in subaccount A (sub-acc-id: sub_7f9) through 2026-03-08; consolidation job completed on 2026-03-09; post-consolidation the consolidated org (org-id: org_bf-consol) shows reduced retained credit balance and the invoice for 2026-03-10 includes no rollover credit line. Expected behavior: credits should be transferred and reflected on consolidated org balance or appear as a prorated credit line on the first post-consolidation invoice. Steps to reproduce (customer flow): 1) Customer opened consolidation flow in Console -> Billing -> Organizations -> Merge subaccounts. 2) Selected sub_7f9 as source and merged into primary org_bf-consol. 3) Confirmed merge on 2026-03-09 02:14 UTC. 4) On 2026-03-10 customer ran a 6-hour batch embedding job and observed credit exhaustion earlier than expected. Logs/artifacts: attached usage-postbacks and postback delivery receipts (timestamped), consolidation audit record from console, and the 2026-03-10 invoice snapshot. Customer included billing export CSV and screen grab of pre-merge retained credits.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: consolidation job executes a transfer of top-level balances then triggers postback processing; if there is an in-flight postback for the source subaccount, the postback may be applied to the old ledger id and lost during merge due to idempotency checks.

Observed that usage-postback processing has a window where ledger id mapping is cached; consolidation invalidates mapping. Postback pb_9832 was timestamped 2026-03-08T23:00:12Z and processed 2026-03-09T02:08:44Z—this is within the merge window (merge at 02:14 UTC). Processing time seems normal but missing ack from billing suggests a downstream write failed or was reconciled to old ledger and then dropped by consolidation cleanup.

Checked job traces: single node in usage-processor showed GC pause at 02:06 causing retry and delayed attempt. The processor retried and used stale ledger reference. Capture: trace link https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/trace/usage/trace-9832

Engineering note: potential race between org-merge workflow and postback processor's ledger resolution cache. Repro attempt: simulated consolidation in staging with scheduled postbacks and confirmed failure mode when consolidation occurs during a retry window.

Impact assessment: affects customers who run consolidation/merge flows while hourly reserve credits or recent postbacks are still in pipeline. Frequency estimated low (<0.5% of merges) but high impact for customers relying on retained credits.

Suggested mitigations: 1) short-term: provisionally apply credit while reconciliation runs (done). 2) mid-term: add strong handoff locking on merge for ledger id resolution or drain in-flight postbacks before committing merge. 3) long-term: make postback processing idempotent to new ledger ids by mapping legacy ledger writes to new parent ledger on detected merge events.
Related artifacts: usage-processor logs (s3://support-artifacts/usage/pb_9832.log), postback delivery receipt (pb_9832.delivery.json), consolidation audit record (audit_2026-03-09-02:14.json).
resolution: 2026-03-14 - Temporary/Workaround: Applied provisional credit of $4,200 to Brightline Freight (visible in Console -> Billing -> Credits). Notified customer and Finance. This prevents immediate workflow disruption for scheduled jobs.

2026-03-14 - Root cause: Race condition between consolidation job and delayed postback processing where a retry used stale ledger mapping; resulting ledger write was dropped during consolidation cleanup. INT-4421 assigned to Accounting/Engineering for replay.

2026-03-16 - Permanent fix plan: Engineering to implement ledger-resolution locking for org-merge (PR referenced: github.com/redwood-inference/organizations/pull/1291) and add a reconciliation job that replays any postbacks targeting deprecated ledger ids into their consolidated parent. Expected rollout: canary 2026-03-22, full rollout 2026-04-01.

Follow-ups: Finance to issue formal credit memo on invoice 2026-03-10 and audit post-merge ledger migration logs. Support to reach back to customer with confirmation once reconciliation completes and the provisional credit converted to invoice adjustment. Ticket will remain open until INT-4421 is closed and invoice adjusted.
